> **Pipeline step 01 — TPS catch models (main text).**
>
> **Purpose.** Fit the 14 TPS water-quality / edge-type negative-binomial catch models
> (`fit_tps_wq0` … `fit_tps_wq13`), score each with moment-matched PSIS-LOO, and write the ELPD
> ranking used by the model-comparison figure and the stacked ensemble.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv` (built by `00_data/01_build_model_datasets.Rmd`).
>
> **Outputs.** `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq<N>.rds`, `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/tps_wq_fits_Vfix_output.txt`,
> `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq1-13_catch_looic_comparisons.csv`.
>
> **Cost.** ~5 min per model on 4 cores; the fitting chunk is `eval=FALSE` and refuses to
> overwrite an existing fit, so knitting this notebook only prints the model set.
>
> **Appendix.** The salinity fits (14–16) and the water-year diagnostic fit (17) re-use the
> runner defined here; they live in
> `appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A03_tps_salinity_wateryear_fits.R`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Water-quality + edge/habitat model set for the TPS (Tidal Parr Survey) trawl catch analysis,
functionalised for reference (dataset built in `00_data/01_build_model_datasets.Rmd`).
This is the companion set to `01_tps_catch_models/tps_catch_landscape_models.Rmd`: same sampler settings,
same negative-binomial + offset structure, but a different dataset
(`tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona`, which adds the water-quality and edge/habitat covariates) and its own
fit directory.

Like the landscape notebook, this analysis stays with PSIS-LOO + moment matching rather than
grouped K-fold CV: each row of `tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona` is an independent tow sample (there is no
`(1|StationCode)` grouping term here), so leave-one-observation-out is the correct
cross-validation unit.

The code is functionalised the same way as the landscape / k-fold notebooks:
  * one `fit_defs` table describes every model (fit 0..13),
  * one runner fits the model, computes moment-matched LOO, saves the full fit, and appends the
    summary to the shared text file,
  * the ELPD/LOOIC comparison at the end reads the saved fits (or, if you build them, the small
    LOO sidecars) and writes the ranking table.

Model set, in the order it was actually built (this is the reasoning trail, not a full factorial):

  * fit 0        — BASE model. `out30_z * distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z`. The landscape
                   model carried forward from the no-WQ analysis; everything below is base + one
                   or more additions.
  * fits 1-6     — ROUND ONE, one covariate at a time on top of the base: habitat class (1),
                   edge type (2), chlorophyll (3), Secchi (4), dissolved oxygen (5), pH (6).
  * fits 7-9     — ROUND TWO. Round one ranked edge type first, then habitat class, then Secchi,
                   then the base model alone; the ELPD differences among base / Secchi /
                   chlorophyll were practically indistinguishable, and DO and pH were marginally
                   worse with similar SEs. So edge type was combined with Secchi (7),
                   chlorophyll (8), and both (9). Habitat class was NOT mixed with edge type:
                   the two do not converge in the same model.
  * fits 10-13   — ROUND THREE. Edge type held, landscape terms dropped back in one at a time
                   (no outflow x distance interaction) to see how much of the base structure the
                   edge effect actually needs: outflow + edge (10), + distance along channel (11),
                   + distance off channel (12), + both distances (13).

Salinity, temperature and water year are NOT part of the reported set. Salinity fits
(14 = base + salinity, 15 = + edge, 16 = + edge + Secchi) and the water-year diagnostic
(17 = fit 16 + factor(water_year)) are fitted with the runner below from
`appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A03_tps_salinity_wateryear_fits.R` and reported in
the appendix only. Salinity is not identifiable against outflow transport in these data:
outflow both carries parr seaward and freshens the water they are carried into.

All predictors are on their raw scale, z-scored; the only log is `offset(log(Volume))`.

Settings (iter = 3000 / warmup = 2000, chains = 4, max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99,
negbinomial, `offset(log(Volume))`) match the landscape and EDSM notebooks so that any difference
in inference reflects the data, not how the models were fit. `save_pars(all = TRUE)` is required
because moment matching needs the auxiliary draws.

NOTE ON REPRODUCTION: the fits reported in the manuscript already exist in `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/`.
The runner below refuses to overwrite an existing fit unless you pass `overwrite = TRUE`, so
re-running this notebook cannot silently replace the published fits.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(loo)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config — single source of truth for paths.
```{r config}
FIT_DIR <- "fits_tps_wq_Vfix"
OUT_TXT <- file.path(FIT_DIR, "tps_wq_fits_Vfix_output.txt")   # appended printout
if (!dir.exists(FIT_DIR)) dir.create(FIT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)
```

Load the TPS water-quality dataset (one independent tow per row; n = 818).

The upstream build (in `00_data/01_build_model_datasets.Rmd`) selects the modelled columns
from the full tow table, drops the `Riprap` edge class (too few tows to estimate), `drop_na()`s,
then z-scores the continuous covariates and derives `water_year_day` / `water_year` from
`SampleDate`. The `_z` columns in the CSV are therefore already centred and scaled on THIS
dataset — do not re-scale them, and do not compare coefficient magnitudes to the landscape or
EDSM fit sets, which were z-scored on their own subsets.
```{r load-data}
tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona <- read_csv("data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv")

# Categorical predictors: brms uses the first level as the reference. Character columns come back
# from read_csv unordered, and factor() defaults to alphabetical, which reproduces the level
# ordering the saved fits were built with -- reference levels "Cut Bank" (Edge_Type) and
# "Distributary" (habitat2020), matching the coefficient names in fits_tps_wq_Vfix/.
tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona <- tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona %>%
  mutate(Edge_Type    = factor(Edge_Type),
         habitat2020  = factor(habitat2020))
```


###################################
Priors.
  * b       normal(0, 5)  — on the z-scored predictor scale. Weakly informative; the fitted
                            estimates all sit well inside it.
  * shape   gamma(2, 0.1) — negative-binomial dispersion.
  * Intercept + sds       — LEFT AT brms DEFAULTS (student_t(3, -10.3, 2.5) and
                            student_t(3, 0, 2.5)). These live on this dataset's own scale
                            (the offset puts the intercept near log catch-per-litre), so the
                            auto-scaled defaults are the right "let the data speak" choice.
Note these are the priors the saved `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/` fits were actually built with; the
landscape notebook tightened `b` to normal(0, 2.5) for its own set.
########################################
```{r priors}
catch_priors <- c(prior(normal(0, 5),   class = "b"),
                  prior(gamma(2, 0.1),  class = "shape"))
```


###################################
LOO helper.
Computes PSIS-LOO with `save_psis = TRUE`, then moment-matches it (`loo_moment_match` needs the
full posterior, hence `save_pars(all = TRUE)` on the fit) and stores it on the fit under
`fit$criteria$loo`, exactly as the original notebook did.
########################################
```{r loo-helpers}
add_loo_mm <- function(fit, moment_match = TRUE, cores = parallel::detectCores()) {
  loo_result <- loo(fit, save_psis = TRUE, cores = cores)
  if (moment_match) {
    loo_result <- loo_moment_match(fit, loo = loo_result, cores = cores)
  }
  fit$criteria$loo <- loo_result
  fit
}

# Slim a loo object down to what loo_compare() / loo_model_weights() actually use
# (estimates + pointwise). The psis_object holds the full 4000 x N log-lik/weights matrix and is
# NOT needed for ranking or stacking; dropping it turns a ~25 MB sidecar into ~60 KB. That
# matters in this iCloud-synced folder, where large .rds files get evicted and then fail to read
# mid-batch ("error reading from connection"). The full loo (with psis_object) still lives inside
# the big fit's $criteria$loo.
slim_loo <- function(loo_obj) {
  loo_obj$psis_object <- NULL
  loo_obj
}

# Robust readRDS for this iCloud-synced folder. If a file has been evicted to the cloud, the
# first read can fail; force macOS to materialize it (brctl download, then fault the bytes in
# with a full read) and retry a few times.
read_rds_icloud <- function(f, tries = 4) {
  for (i in seq_len(tries)) {
    obj <- tryCatch(readRDS(f), error = function(e) e)
    if (!inherits(obj, "error")) return(obj)
    try(system2("brctl", c("download", shQuote(f)), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE), silent = TRUE)
    invisible(tryCatch(readBin(f, "raw", file.info(f)$size), error = function(e) NULL))  # fault in
    Sys.sleep(1.5)
  }
  stop("could not read ", f, " after ", tries, " tries (iCloud eviction?).")
}
```


###################################
Model definition table + runner.
`fit_defs` lists the fixed-effects part of each model (fit 0..13), transcribed verbatim from the
original hand-written chunks. The base model appended to each is:
  n_l_75 ~ <fixef> + s(water_year_day) + offset(log(Volume))
`round` and `note` carry the build rationale described in the header; they are documentation
only and do not affect the fit.
########################################
```{r fit-defs-runner}
BASE_FIXEF <- "out30_z*distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z"

fit_defs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~num, ~round, ~fixef,                                                        ~note,
  0L,   "base", BASE_FIXEF,                                                    "landscape base model",
  1L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ habitat2020"),                            "base + habitat class",
  2L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ Edge_Type"),                              "base + edge type",
  3L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ chlorophyll_z"),                          "base + chlorophyll",
  4L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ secchi_z"),                               "base + Secchi",
  5L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ dox_z"),                                  "base + dissolved oxygen",
  6L,   "one",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ ph_z"),                                   "base + pH",
  7L,   "two",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ Edge_Type + secchi_z"),                   "base + edge + Secchi",
  8L,   "two",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ Edge_Type + chlorophyll_z"),              "base + edge + chlorophyll",
  9L,   "two",  paste(BASE_FIXEF, "+ Edge_Type + secchi_z + chlorophyll_z"),   "base + edge + Secchi + chlorophyll",
  10L,  "three","out30_z + Edge_Type",                                         "outflow + edge",
  11L,  "three","out30_z + distance_along_channel_z + Edge_Type",              "outflow + dist along channel + edge",
  12L,  "three","out30_z + distance_m_z + Edge_Type",                          "outflow + dist off channel + edge",
  13L,  "three","out30_z + distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z + Edge_Type","outflow + both distances + edge"
)
# (Appendix fits 14-17 are defined in appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A03_*.R.)

# Build the full brms formula for a given fixed-effects string.
build_tps_wq_formula <- function(fixef) {
  rhs <- c(fixef, "s(water_year_day)", "offset(log(Volume))")
  rhs <- rhs[nzchar(trimws(rhs))]
  as.formula(paste("n_l_75 ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Inspect the model set without fitting anything.
show_fit_defs <- function(defs = fit_defs) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(defs))) {
    cat(sprintf("fit_tps_wq%-2d [round %-5s] %s\n    %s\n",
                defs$num[i], defs$round[i], defs$note[i],
                deparse1(build_tps_wq_formula(defs$fixef[i]))))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Fit ONE model, compute moment-matched LOO, save the full fit (+ optionally a lightweight LOO
# sidecar), append the summary, free memory.
# overwrite = FALSE (default) is a guard: the reported fits already exist in fits_tps_wq_Vfix/
# and must not be silently replaced. Pass overwrite = TRUE only if you really mean to refit.
fit_tps_wq_model <- function(num, fixef,
                             data         = tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona,
                             priors       = catch_priors,
                             iter         = 3000,
                             warmup       = 2000,
                             chains       = 4,
                             control      = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
                             dir          = FIT_DIR,
                             out_txt      = OUT_TXT,
                             overwrite    = FALSE,
                             save_sidecar = FALSE) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("fit_tps_wq%d.rds", num))
  if (file.exists(fit_file) && !overwrite) {
    message("SKIP fit_tps_wq", num, ": ", fit_file,
            " already exists (pass overwrite = TRUE to refit).")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  form <- build_tps_wq_formula(fixef)
  message("=== Fitting fit_tps_wq", num, " ===")
  print(form)

  fit <- brm(
    formula = form,
    family  = negbinomial(link = "log"),
    data    = data,
    prior   = priors,
    iter    = iter, warmup = warmup, chains = chains,
    control = control,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )

  fit <- add_loo_mm(fit)

  # Full fit (posterior draws -> conditional effects / CIs / forest plots / ensemble weighting)
  saveRDS(fit, file = fit_file)
  # Optional lightweight LOO criterion (ELPD -> ranking) without loading the big fit.
  if (save_sidecar) {
    saveRDS(slim_loo(fit$criteria$loo), file = file.path(dir, sprintf("loo_tps_wq%d.rds", num)))
  }

  # Append the summary to the shared printout file (same file as the original notebook).
  fileConn <- file(out_txt, open = "a")
  cat(sprintf("\n\n\nSummary of fit_tps_wq%d:\n\n", num), file = fileConn)
  cat(capture.output(summary(fit)), file = fileConn, sep = "\n")
  close(fileConn)

  rm(fit); gc()
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Loop over a set of fit numbers (default: all 14, fit 0..13).
run_tps_wq_fits <- function(nums = fit_defs$num, defs = fit_defs, ...) {
  unknown <- setdiff(nums, defs$num)
  if (length(unknown)) {
    stop("No fixed-effects definition for fit number(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }
  for (num in nums) {
    fixef <- defs$fixef[match(num, defs$num)]
    fit_tps_wq_model(num = num, fixef = fixef, ...)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

Print the model set (cheap — no fitting).
```{r show-defs}
show_fit_defs()
```


###################################
Run the fits.
Each fit + moment-matched LOO is slow (~5 min each on 4 cores); run this interactively, not on
knit. The overwrite guard means this is a no-op against the existing `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/` set.
########################################
```{r run-fits, eval=FALSE}
# Run all 14 (or pass a subset, e.g. run_tps_wq_fits(c(0, 2, 11))).
run_tps_wq_fits(nums = 0:13)
```


###################################
Reload LOO results and rank models by ELPD / LOOIC.
The published fits store their moment-matched LOO inside the fit object (`$criteria$loo`), so the
comparison reads the fits themselves — one at a time, extracting only the small LOO object and
dropping the ~29 MB fit before moving on, so peak memory stays flat instead of holding all 14
fits at once (the original notebook loaded them all into the global environment).
If you have built the slim sidecars, `load_loo_tps_wq(..., prefer_sidecar = TRUE)` will use those
instead and skip the big files entirely.
########################################
```{r load-loo-fn}
load_loo_tps_wq <- function(nums = fit_defs$num, dir = FIT_DIR, prefer_sidecar = FALSE) {
  out <- list()
  for (num in nums) {
    side <- file.path(dir, sprintf("loo_tps_wq%d.rds", num))
    if (prefer_sidecar && file.exists(side)) {
      out[[paste0("fit_tps_wq", num)]] <- read_rds_icloud(side)
      next
    }
    f <- file.path(dir, sprintf("fit_tps_wq%d.rds", num))
    if (!file.exists(f)) {
      warning("missing fit: ", f); next
    }
    fit <- read_rds_icloud(f)
    if (!is.null(fit$criteria$loo)) {
      out[[paste0("fit_tps_wq", num)]] <- fit$criteria$loo
    } else {
      warning("no $criteria$loo on ", f)
    }
    rm(fit); gc()
  }
  out
}
```

```{r compare-loo, eval=FALSE}
fit_nums <- 0:13

loo_results <- load_loo_tps_wq(fit_nums)

if (length(loo_results) < 2) {
  stop("Need at least two fits with LOO results to compare; run the fits first.")
}

# ELPD / LOOIC comparison ranking (best model on top, elpd_diff relative to it)
looic_comparisons <- loo_compare(loo_results)
print(looic_comparisons)

write.csv(
  as.data.frame(looic_comparisons),
  file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit_tps_wq1-13_catch_looic_comparisons.csv")
)
```

The published ranking is in `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq1-13_catch_looic_comparisons.csv`
(and `..._notes.csv`, the same table annotated with which covariates each model carries). It puts
fit 11 (outflow + distance along channel + edge type) on top, with fit 13 (adding distance off
channel) 1.5 ELPD behind — i.e. distance along channel and edge type are the terms that buy
predictive performance, and the water-quality covariates do not separate from the base model.

Stacking weights and model-averaged conditional effects for this fit set are computed downstream
in `05_figures/main_text_ensemble_figures.Rmd`, not here.
